title: Job 14
paragraphs: ¹ A person born of woman has few days and much trouble. ² They come up like a flower, then wither; they flee like a shadow and do not last. ³ Do you really open your eyes on such a person? Do you really bring me into judgment with you? ⁴ Who can bring a clean thing out of an unclean? No one. ⁵ A person's days are determined; you know the number of their months; you have set limits they cannot go beyond.

⁶ Look away from them and let them rest, until — like a hired worker — they have completed their day. ⁷ There is hope for a tree: if it is cut down, it will sprout again, and its new shoots will keep coming. ⁸ Though its root grows old in the ground and its stump dies in the soil, ⁹ at the scent of water it will bud again and put out branches like a young plant. ¹⁰ But a person dies and lies still; they breathe their last, and then where are they?

¹¹ As water vanishes from a lake, and a river drains away and dries up, ¹² so a person lies down and does not rise again; until the heavens are no more, they will not awake, and they will not be roused from their sleep. ¹³ Oh, that you would hide me in the grave, that you would conceal me until your anger has passed, and set a time for me and then remember me! ¹⁴ If a man dies, will he live again? All the days of my hard labor I would wait, hoping for my release.

¹⁶ For now you count my every step; you watch over my sin. ¹⁷ My transgression is sealed up in a bag, and you sew up my guilt. ¹⁸ Yet as a mountain crumbles away and falls, and as a rock shifts from its place, ¹⁹ as water wears away stones, as floods sweep away the topsoil of the ground — so you destroy a person's hope. ²⁰ You overpower them once and for all, and they are gone; you change their appearance and send them away.

²¹ Their children come to honor, and they do not know it; their children are brought low, and they do not see it. ²² Only this do they feel: their own body's pain; only this do they mourn: themselves.
